 Live .  62,040 viewing 62040 viewing Live page Updated 7 minutes ago Russell Brand sentenced to 10 years and six months for rape and sexual assault
 Summary
 Warning: This page contains distressing details 
 Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10-and-a-half years for rape and three counts of sexual assault - he is likely to serve two-thirds of the sentence in prison 
 The judge tells Brand he is a "sexual predator" , who told a "series of lies" and displayed "staggering arrogance" 
 Earlier, one victim told the court she was "in shock and turmoil... I didn't have any respect for myself" 
 Another victim said "Russell Brand is a sexual predator who has no remorse" , while another said she "felt powerless in that moment" 
 The woman who Brand raped in 2009 told the court she was "living with trauma" , and feared she had contracted HIV 
 Brand faced seven charges: three of rape, three of sexual assault and one of attempted indecent assault. He was found not guilty on three counts
 His crimes took place between 2004 and 2009, and related to four women. They are all entitled to lifelong anonymity

 Live Reporting
 Edited by Nathan Williams, with Helena Wilkinson and Sima Kotecha at Southwark Crown Court. Warning: this page contains distressing details
 No emotion from Brand when was handed a substantial sentence published at 16:21 GMT 16:21 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 When Brand was handed his substantial sentence in Court 1 at
Southwark Crown Court, he simply stood and looked ahead.
 There was no emotion.
 Today he seemed more relaxed in the dock compared to the
statue-like posture he kept for much of the trial. At one point he did the sign
of the cross and was holding what looked like prayer beads.
 Today though the focus has been on the four women. We
already knew their stories, and today we heard about the "turmoil"
and "trauma" Brand caused.
 And then came the words of the judge; he called Brand a
"sexual predator".
 But it was this line that the judge said that really stood
out:
 "Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever
they drink, they retain the right to say no and to demand justice from the
criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Russell Brand, act without
their consent."

 Fame Under Fire: The BBC's podcast about the Russell Brand trial published at 15:59 GMT 15:59 GMT 
 Fame Under Fire, a podcast from BBC Sounds, has been following the Russell Brand trial as it unfolded.
 Across more than 20 episodes, it looks at how police built their case, how the trial played out across three weeks at Southwark Crown Court, and summarises statements from those who gave evidence.
 The podcast is available on BBC Sounds, YouTube and iPlayer - for a full list of episodes, you can click here .

 Sentencing demonstrates 'why investigative journalism matters' - Channel 4 boss published at 15:41 GMT 15:41 GMT 
 Channel 4's Dispatches programme says the sentencing of
Russell Brand is a "powerful demonstration of why investigative journalism
matters".
 The programme – alongside journalists from the Sunday Times
and the Times – in 2023 first exposed a litany of sexual misconduct by Brand,
leading to women making complaints to police.
 In a statement, director of news Louisa Compton pays tribute
to the "courage of these women who gave evidence through the criminal
justice system".
 "Today, and throughout the trial, we have heard of the
trauma suffered by the women in this case," she says.
 "Above all else, we commend their bravery."

 Judge calls Brand a 'sexual predator' as he's sentenced to 10-and-a-half years - a recap published at 15:23 GMT 15:23 GMT 
 Media caption, Watch: Moment judge sentences Brand to 10 years and six months in jail
 Judge Mr Justice Bennathan opened his sentencing remarks by describing Russell Brand as a "sexual predator". 
 First, the judge talked about a sexual assault that took place in a bar in Soho in 2004 - he said that Brand's claim during the trial that he had "never touched a woman without her consent" was one of a "series of lies". 
 Moving on to a sexual assault against a woman at the Choice FM studios in 2004 or 2005, where Brand grabbed the victim's face and kissed her before touching her breasts and bottom, the judge said this was sustained and there was added humiliation in front of others.
 Addressing the rape in 2009, the judge said when Brand ordered the victim to clean his sheets, it was a "humiliation".
 Justice Bennathan said the sexual assault by Brand at Channel 4 in 2009 yet again showed his "staggering arrogance", adding: "Your entourage indulged your dreadful behaviour." 
 The judge then moved to sentence Brand to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault.
 Brand did not react to the sentence, our reporter in court described , but he mouthed to his wife "I love you". 
 Image source, Elizabeth Cook/PA

 Prison van leaves Southwark Crown Court published at 15:13 GMT 15:13 GMT 
 A large white prison van has been filmed leaving Southwark Crown Court.
 Photographers are crowding the windows trying to get pictures of inside - it's unclear if Russell Brand is in the van. 
 Image source, BBC/Helena Wilkinson

 Police and CPS deliver statements outside court - watch live published at 15:05 GMT 15:05 GMT Breaking 
 Det Supt Andy Furphy from the Metropolitan Police and David Roberts from the Crown Prosecution Service are delivering statements outside Southwark Crown Court.
 You can watch live at the top of this page. 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Sentence 'cannot undo the harm the victims have lived with', CPS prosecutor says published at 15:05 GMT 15:05 GMT 
 In a written statement, Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) senior crown prosecutor David Roberts thanks the women who were "at the heart of this case":
 "They did not know each other, and each has carried what happened to them for almost two decades," he says.
 Giving evidence in the trial and being questioned about these "deeply traumatising, personal events" took extraordinary courage, he says.
 Roberts adds that, while today’s sentence "cannot undo the harm the victims have lived with", he hopes it brings them some measure of justice.
 The trial showed Brand to be a "manipulative sexual predator, using his growing fame and power to create situations in which he could pursue
 women sexually, regardless of what they wanted and with a complete disregard for the impact of his actions", Roberts says. 
 He adds: "Today’s result shows that fame, status and the passage of time do not change the fundamental issue of consent.
 "No matter who the abuser is, or what the situation or circumstances are, we will always take allegations of rape and sexual assault seriously."

 Brand's wife pictured leaving court published at 14:59 GMT 14:59 GMT 
 Image source, Reuters Image source, Getty Images Russell Brand's wife Laura was seen leaving Southwark Crown Court a short while ago, flanked by supporters.
 Her husband's lawyer said in court earlier that she was experiencing "total devastation."

 Met Police detective thanks women for 'bravery, dignity and resilience' published at 14:55 GMT 14:55 GMT 
 We can now bring you a statement from Det Supt Andy Furphy, of the Metropolitan Police.
 He says the sentence is a "significant milestone", and means Brand has been held accountable for his crimes. 
 Furphy says his thoughts are with the women who came forward and made the investigation possible, adding that they displayed "bravery, dignity and resilience" throughout the process. 
 "The victims have had to revisit deeply traumatic experiences and endure significant public and media attention. I hope today’s outcome provides some measure of closure and allows them to continue rebuilding their lives," he says.
 Furphy adds: "From the very beginning, our investigation was never about Russell Brand’s profile, status or celebrity. 
 "Our focus has always been on the women who reported these offences and on conducting a thorough and impartial investigation into the allegations they made."
 He ends with an appeal to anyone who has been a victim of rape or any other sexual offence. "If you come forward, you will be listened to, supported and treated with care and compassion," he says. 
 Image source, Reuters Image caption, Andy Furphy, speaking to the media after Brand was found guilty on Thursday

 Large crowds of media and public outside court published at 14:52 GMT 14:52 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Image source, BBC/Helena Wilkinson Outside court there are huge crowds and media.
 We are currently waiting for statements from the Metropolitan Police and the Crown Prosecution Service.
 We are also expecting Laura Brand to leave court after hearing her husband’s sentence of 10 years and six months.

 I'm conscious prison will deprive you from children... but it's your own fault, judge tells Brand published at 14:48 GMT 14:48 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Let's return briefly to the remarks made by the judge before he handed down Brand's sentence. 
 The judge said the statement in Brand’s support from a friend was "particularly impressive".
 He said: "I’m also conscious you being in prison will deprive you from your children."
 But, he told Brand, that’s very much his own fault.
 The judge said it's his view it would be wrong to disregard Brand’s mitigation, and said the sentence was reduced by one year as a result.

 Brand's friends in tears outside court published at 14:42 GMT 14:42 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Russell Brand’s friends can be seen crying outside the court, after hearing the sentence be handed down.
 A woman can be seen wiping away tears.

 A breakdown of Russell Brand's sentence published at 14:40 GMT 14:40 GMT 
 In total, Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months. 
 He has been sentenced to nine years' imprisonment for the one count of rape, which he will serve consecutively with the following three sentences:
 Nine months for count three - sexually assaulting a woman whose breasts he grabbed at a bar in London in 2004
 Eighteen months for count five - sexually assaulting a woman at the Choice FM studios in London in either 2004 or 2005, when he grabbed her face and kissed her before touching her breasts and bottom
 Eight months for count seven - sexual assault while working on a Channel 4 project in 2009, when he laid his head into the groin area of a woman working with him without her consent 
 These three sentences will all be served concurrently to one another - but consecutively to the rape sentence.
 This means the total sentence is one of 10 years and six months.
 Media caption, Moment judge sentences Brand to 10 years and six months in jail
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Likely Brand will serve two-thirds of sentence in custody published at 14:36 GMT 14:36 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Brand is likely to serve two-thirds of his sentence in custody according to the Sentencing Council.
 The council states offenders jailed for four years or more for some serious violent or sexual offences will be released at the two-thirds point.
 Once released, he is likely to spend the rest of his sentence on licence and will have to abide by specific rules - such as wearing a tag.
 His sentence will not be included in the new early release scheme. Sex offenders - along with murderers - are exempt from the scheme.

 Brand tells wife 'I love you' as he is taken to cells published at 14:29 GMT 14:29 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Brand doesn't react to his substantial sentence, and is taken down to the cells.
 He stops for a moment to mouth to his wife: "I love you."

 Brand sentenced to 10 years and six months published at 14:26 GMT 14:26 GMT Breaking 
 Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault.
 We'll bring you more on the judge's remarks shortly.

 Actions show Brand's 'staggering arrogance', judge says published at 14:23 GMT 14:23 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson and Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 The judge moves on to talk about a sexual assault against a woman at the Choice FM studios in London in either 2004 or 2005.
 This is where Brand grabbed the victim's face and kissed her before touching her breasts and bottom. 
 The judge says this was sustained and there was added humiliation in front of others.
 He reads from the victim impact statement: "It was rough - very, very rough - he squeezed my breast. I looked at the woman and she said nothing."
 Addressing the rape in 2009, the judge says when Brand ordered the victim to clean his sheets, it was a "humiliation".
 He says the sexual assault by Brand at Channel 4 in 2009 yet again shows his "staggering arrogance".
 "Your entourage indulged your dreadful behaviour," he says.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Judge says Brand told a 'series of lies' published at 14:18 GMT 14:18 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson and Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 The judge is talking about the sexual assault that took place in a bar in Soho.
 He says that, during the trial, Brand said he had "never touched a woman without her consent".
 That was one of a "series of lies you told", the judge says.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Sentences won't all run consecutively, judge says published at 14:16 GMT 14:16 GMT 
 Mr Justice Bennathan says the sentencing guidance means he "shall not make all sentences consequently to one another".
 But, he says, Brand committed sexual offences against a number
of women over a five-year period. 
 If I were to make all the sentences concurrent (i.e. all running at the same time, rather than added together), he says, "that would
not do justice to the overall gravity of your criminality".
 He adds that when passing several sentences that the overall result is just and proportionate.

 Brand's wife looks at the floor as judge speaks published at 14:13 GMT 14:13 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Laura Brand, Russell Brand’s wife, is looking at the floor as the judge speaks - occasionally glancing towards her husband in the dock.
 She is sitting behind him so can’t see his face.
